chief_complaint: Elevated diastolic blood pressure (stage 2 hypertension) with associated metabolic risk factors

Most recent vital signs (2020-05-16) show isolated diastolic hypertension (DBP 103 mmHg) despite a normal systolic pressure. A1c is 6.1%, indicating prediabetes. She reports ongoing unhealthy alcohol use and chronic stress, and she is a victim of intimate partner abuse. No emergency or inpatient visits have been recorded; outpatient and wellness visits have been routine but the last encounter was in May 2020, suggesting possible data staleness.

She previously experienced stress (resolved 2019-01-05) and was unemployed (resolved 2019-01-05). She was not in the labor force (resolved 2017-12-30).
social_determinants: Refugee background, criminal record, high school education, full-time employment, ongoing intimate partner abuse, chronic stress, and unhealthy alcohol use. These factors likely impact healthcare access, medication adherence, and overall disease management.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 diastolic hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, unhealthy alcohol use, chronic stress, and intimate partner violence place the patient at high 10‑year ASCVD risk. Metabolic risk: obesity and prediabetes suggest metabolic syndrome and risk for type 2 diabetes and NAFLD. Renal risk: hypertension and prediabetes without current eGFR or albumin data; ACE inhibitor may be protective but labs are missing. Hematologic risk: longstanding anemia of unclear etiology. Psychosocial risk: refugee status, intimate partner abuse, alcohol misuse, and criminal record increase vulnerability to poor outcomes. Data gaps (BMI, lipids, renal function, smoking status) limit precise risk quantification.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing; obesity is inferred from diagnosis only.
Lipid panel not available; essential for ASCVD risk assessment.
Only one medication captured despite multiple chronic conditions; likely incomplete.
No iron studies, B12, folate, or occult blood testing documented.
No AST/ALT or other liver labs despite alcohol use and obesity.

clinical_impression: Middle-aged woman with a high‑risk cardiovascular and metabolic profile driven by isolated diastolic hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, chronic alcohol use, and significant psychosocial stressors including intimate partner violence. Anemia of uncertain etiology adds to overall clinical complexity. Data gaps in labs and medication list limit full assessment, but the patient warrants intensified risk factor modification, comprehensive metabolic and renal evaluation, and psychosocial support.
